narrative:
Inventory optimization analysis for material PL1__ME7C926E reveals significant opportunities for cost reduction 
and service level improvement. Based on 130 working-day observations spanning March 2025 to March 2026, the 
analysis identifies a smooth demand pattern (CV=0.54, 93% non-zero fraction) with moderate lead time variability 
(CV=0.38, mean=4.0 days).

The current SAP policy maintains a safety stock of 208 units with a minimum order quantity of 208, resulting in 
411 orders per year and a total annual cost of $41,694.61. The optimized policy recommends increasing safety 
stock to 1,052 units (reflecting true demand variability) and order quantity to 2,314 units (EOQ-based), reducing 
order frequency to 37 times per year.

This optimization achieves $34,174.79 in annual cost savings (82.0% reduction), primarily by dramatically reducing 
ordering costs from $41,155 to $3,699 while moderately increasing holding costs from $540 to $3,821. The reorder 
point is set at 2,955 units with a 7-day review period.

The current 4-day safety lead time can be reduced to 3.1 days based on empirical lead time distribution. Two 
extreme lead time outliers (9201 and 9327 days) were removed from analysis; transport variability dominates 
(60%) the lead time uncertainty. The policy is capacity-feasible (max storage: 3,366 units).

Key risks: Moderate lead time variability requires ongoing supplier performance monitoring. No demand trend 
detected, supporting static model assumptions.

research_insights.selected_model: Normal Approximation for Lead Time Demand
research_insights.selection_rationale: CV of 0.54 and non-zero fraction of 0.93 indicate smooth demand suitable for Normal approximation. Gamma distribution would be alternative for CV > 0.7.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Demand regime classified as 'smooth'. Close to erratic boundary if CV increases. Monitor for intermittency if non-zero fraction drops below 0.8.
